Top-level reactions:
- Onshore replicas: we can provide EU-region primary hosting for customer data. For replicas we need to confirm whether NovaTech requires synchronous replication or asynchronous snapshots — synchronous affects latency and cost.

Emma / Vanessa — Ben here. I've reviewed the blackline with the runtime and infra leads and pulled together concrete operational responses below. Inline notes follow key blackline requests.

1) EU replicas:
- Option A (recommended): primary hosting in eu-west-1 with asynchronous cross-region backups to us-west for DR; preserves EU residency for active data and meets latency SLAs.
- Option B: synchronous multi-region replication — possible but will introduce 15–40ms additional median p99 tail latency depending on region pairs and will increase monthly unit costs ~18–25%.

2) 30-day forensic logs carveout:
- We can scope logs by type: "inference telemetry" (latency, token counts, model id) vs "payload logs" (payloads customer submitted). For privacy reasons, we keep payload logs in encrypted form; automatic retention is 14 days for payloads and 90 days for aggregated telemetry by default.
- To support a 30-day forensic window for payloads we can provide an opt-in workflow that enables an extended retention flag per account; this requires a signed request from NovaTech and will be billed as an add-on.

3) Tamper-evident erasure certificate for backups:
- We can issue a signed erasure manifest (JSON manifest hashed and timestamped, signed with Redwood KMS) for snapshots we manage. For backups stored with cloud-provider managed snapshot lifecycles (e.g., provider-managed cold archives), we can provide attestations of deletion initiation and retention expiration but cannot provide the same tamper-evident proof without provider support.

Action items from infra:
- We need NovaTech to confirm whether the 30-day carveout applies to all accounts or only to specific product environments (prod vs non-prod).
- Please confirm whether NovaTech requires evidence for on-demand erasure of backups (post-termination) or periodic certified erasures only.

Attachment: [redline_summary.xlsx (operations mapping, 12KB)]

Happy to hop on a quick call to walk through tradeoffs.

--
Ben Carter
Technical Account Manager, Redwood Inference

Emma — Priya from privacy here. A few legal/controls clarifications to help tighten the DPA language (inline guidance below):

- Residency wording: instead of committing to "onshore replicas in the EU," suggest language that specifies "primary processing and customer-accessible replicas will be located in eu-west-1; cross-border backups are permitted only under the scenarios listed in Appendix X." That aligns better with how our control plane routes replicas and avoids implying synchronous cross-border replication as default.

- Retention carveout duration: if NovaTech insists on 30 days for payload logs, we should define a process to limit scope (e.g., retention applies only to named log classes and accounts) and include an opt-in signed instruction as Ben suggested. Also include an account-level dashboard flag for NovaTech to monitor and revoke the flag.

- Erasure certificate definition: propose to replace "tamper-evident erasure certificate" with a defined artifact name in the agreement: "Redwood Erasure Manifest" consisting of (a) manifest of deleted resources, (b) SHA256 hash signed by Redwood KMS, (c) timestamp and retention TTL of the manifest. Specify that evidence for third-party-managed archives will be provided as best-effort attestations.

Jonas, can legal draft a suggested paragraph along these lines for the DPA?

Thanks,
Priya Natarajan
Privacy Counsel, Redwood Inference

Thanks — this is helpful and close to what we need. A few clarifications from NovaTech legal/procurement:

- The 30-day carveout will apply only to payload logs for customer support investigations (not to aggregated telemetry). We'll provide a list of account IDs that should be flagged when we engage the workflow.
- For the erasure manifest: PDF with signed SHA256 is acceptable if it includes the resource identifiers and timestamps. We prefer an automated delivery channel (SFTP or secure Drive link) when manifests are produced.
- For onshore replicas: NovaTech will accept primary processing in eu-west-1 with a contractual guarantee that active customer data will not be served from non-EU regions except for temporary failover and emergency DR events which must be logged and notified within 24 hours.

Next steps:
1) Redwood to provide redline paragraph language for the three items above (retention opt-in workflow, Redwood Erasure Manifest definition, emergency DR notification window).
2) We will run these language changes through NovaTech procurement and legal; hope to finalize by end of next week.
